threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 73 bus will be reliable; everyone else has a backup plan since it's always late or just doesn't show.
Saw a guy on the N37 serenading the whole bus with old reggae tunes. Everyone was surprisingly into it; even the driver tapped the steering wheel.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a kid in a dirndl selling homemade pretzels outside the Späti during Oktoberfest. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a techno club in an old slaughterhouse, where the beats drop harder than the temperature outside in February.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local when they can navigate the pothole minefield on 16th without missing a beat, but tourists are out here dodging like it’s a game.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, I saw a guy serenading Muni riders with a ukulele at Civic Center—complete with an impromptu dance from an elderly lady. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's just about the parks and plazas, but the real charm is in the back streets where the locals chat over morning coffee, not selfies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new when they stand in line at the bakery for a whole baguette instead of just asking for a ‘barra’.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You know someone’s new when they still think Hackney is just trendy cafés and boutiques, not a battleground for Tube strike chaos.
Caught the 196 last night, and the driver had a proper chat with an elderly couple about their garden. Never seen that kind of warmth on a night bus before.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids using the bus shelter as a stage for their breakdancing. That’s when I knew this place has a pulse.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find random techno parties in abandoned buildings, where the sound systems are better than some clubs. Pure Berlin vibes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only the locals know it’s not a ‘sourdough bread’ but a ‘San Francisco sourdough’—and that’s a big difference when ordering at the bakery.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo trying to woo his date on a crowded Muni bus, all while avoiding a skateboarder weaving through passengers. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think ‘tap a bar’ is all nightlife. In Gràcia, it’s about the quiet corners and street art, not just the bar crawl.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they struggle with tipping—leaving 10 cents on a €5 coffee like it’s an insult.
